title: Next Permutation
prompt: Given an array of integers `nums`, rearrange it into the lexicographically next greater permutation of numbers in place. If no such permutation exists (the array is the highest possible permutation), rearrange it to the lowest possible order (sorted ascending). You must do this in place using only constant extra memory.

examples.explanation: 3,2,1 is the highest permutation, so it wraps to the lowest.

hints: The next permutation changes the smallest possible suffix of the array — the rightmost part that can be rearranged to something larger.

Scan from the right to find the first index i where nums[i] < nums[i+1]; everything after i is already in descending order (the largest suffix arrangement) and needs to be 'incremented' at position i.
Once you find that pivot, swap it with the smallest value to its right that's still larger than it, then reverse the entire suffix after the pivot to put it in the smallest (ascending) order.

solution.approach: Scan from the right to find the first index i (the pivot) where nums[i] < nums[i+1] — everything to the right of i is in descending order, meaning that suffix is already at its maximum arrangement and must 'roll over.' If such a pivot exists, scan from the right again to find the smallest value greater than nums[i] (the first one larger, since the suffix is descending) and swap it with nums[i], which produces the smallest possible increase at that position. Finally, reverse the suffix after i to put it back in ascending (minimal) order. If no pivot exists, the whole array is descending (the last permutation), so simply reverse it entirely to wrap to the first permutation.
